concept: FDE Case Studies: Outcomes And Evidence
title: FDE Case Studies: Outcomes And Evidence Checkpoint

questions.prompt: The Morgan Stanley story reports over 98% of advisor teams using the assistant. What does that describe?

options.label: Reported team adoption, not a 98% answer-accuracy rate.
A controlled demonstration that every answer is correct.
A guaranteed usage rate for any new customer.

questions.explanation: The published metric concerns team use. It does not establish answer accuracy, causality or transferable adoption guarantees.

questions.prompt: A story reports 51% average resolution and up to 86%. How should a new pilot use those numbers?

options.label: Average 51 and 86 to predict its own result.
Keep the statistics distinct and measure its own defined workload.

questions.explanation: Average and maximum describe different statistics and populations. Neither a minimum promise nor their arithmetic average predicts a new deployment.

questions.prompt: Airbus describes eliminating technical delays as a long-term aim in a 2018 release. What can you claim?

options.label: The release proves current fleet-wide causal savings.
It was a stated historical ambition, not proof that all such delays were eliminated.
Every easyJet delay was eliminated by the announcement date.

questions.explanation: Plans and reported trial outcomes must remain separate. A dated announcement cannot establish unreported completion or a current causal estimate.

questions.prompt: A successful customer case resembles your project. What is the next useful artifact?

options.label: A transfer hypothesis, missing-evidence list and local experiment.
A copied performance guarantee using the vendor's best number.
A claim that the same architecture must fit every customer.

questions.explanation: Case studies inspire testable hypotheses. Different data, users and constraints prevent automatic transfer of outcomes or architecture.
